Council votes 6–1 to put protected bike lanes on Alder Street
Harlow will get its first protected bike lanes next spring after the City Council voted 6–1 on Tuesday night to rebuild a 1.8-mile stretch of Alder Street between the train depot and Lakeview Park.

The $4.2 million plan swaps one lane of traffic in each direction for a curb-separated bike lane, adds raised crosswalks at six intersections and keeps most of the street’s parking. Work is set to start in April and wrap up before school starts in August.

Supporters packed the chamber for more than three hours of public comment. Parents from Alder Elementary described kids weaving between delivery trucks, and the owner of Second Gear Cycles said rentals had doubled since the city painted temporary lanes last summer.

Not everyone was sold. Several shop owners near Fifth Avenue worried that losing a lane would slow deliveries and push customers to the mall off Route 9. Councilmember Ray Okafor, the lone no vote, said the city should have studied a one-way plan first.

City engineer Lauren Pike said the design keeps a loading zone on every block, and that crews will hold at least one lane open each way while they work. A last round of open houses is planned for January at the Harlow Public Library.

Federal grants will cover about 60 percent of the cost, with the rest coming from the city’s road fund. Mayor Ellen Brandt called the vote “a long time coming” and said she hopes to extend the lanes north to the high school by 2028.
The council voted 6–1 for protected bike lanes on 1.8 miles of Alder Street.
The $4.2M rebuild starts in April and should be done by August.
